stance.label: US chips sell off again · S&P 500 still above its 200-day line · stay on plan

headline: SOX plunges 5.3%, TSMC ADR falls 6.3%, Nasdaq enters correction; Taiwan tries to steady today
summary: Last night was more chip selling, not a turn in the broad US market: the S&P 500 fell 1.9% but stays above its 200-day line, and no systemic lights are on. The pressure sits in semiconductors, and new US chip export rules add to it. Taiwan night futures rose 154 points, so today the question is whether Taiwan stops falling. Nvidia reports early Wednesday Taipei time. Keep regular investing on plan.

overview.lead: Chips led a broad US selloff last night, but the index fell only a third as much: the SOX lost 5.3%, the S&P 500 1.9%.
points: The Nasdaq fell 2.5% and is now more than 10% below its October high, a correction.
Nvidia (NVDA) fell another 4.1% to $156; the CEO shake-up still weighs on it.
Micron (MU) fell 7.6% and AMD (AMD) 5.6%; memory and AI chips sold off together.
TSMC's ADR (TSM) fell 6.3%, more than the SOX.
The equal-weight S&P 500 (RSP) fell only 1%; the selling was in big tech.
Consumer staples and utilities edged up, the only shelter last night.

focus.lead: Among the nine, US tech is under the most strain: QQQ fell 2.7% and is 2.4% from tier 3. The two Taiwan funds' 11/16 NAVs already show Monday's crash.
points: QQQ closed 3% below its 200-day line, while SPY is still above.
SPY fell 1.9% but is still 1% above its 200-day line; the uptrend call holds.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV fell 8.4% on 11/16, about 30% below its high.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) NAV fell 7.8% on 11/16, now 6% below its 200-day line.
The two Taiwan funds share 6 top-10 names, about 27% of weight, so they fall almost in step.
NAV dates: Fidelity Japan Value, Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan and both AB funds are at 11/13, before these two days of chip selling.

position.lead: No new tier was hit last night; the closest is QQQ tier 3, 2.4% away.
points: QQQ has hit two tiers; tier 3 at 645.71 is 2.4% away.
SPY tier 2 at 701.18 is 5.2% away.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) tier 5 at 1,219 is 10.9% away (11/13 NAV).
0050 tier 5 at 81.55 is 15.4% away.
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used all tiers; further NAV drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: Rates and regulation both weigh on tech: the 10-year yield is above 5%, and a Fed governor flagged corporate debt.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.12%, still high at the long end.
Fed Governor Bowman turned hawkish on corporate debt, a worry for tech giants borrowing to build data centers.
High-yield spreads are 3.2% (11/13); credit markets are calm.
Brent fell back to about $92 as Strait of Hormuz shipping recovered.
The Taiwan dollar is at 32.87 (11/13), 0.7 weaker in a month, not a sharp drop.

sentiment.lead: US mood has turned to fear, not panic: the VIX rose to 22.9 and no bottoming signals are on.
points: The VIX rose 3.6 in a day, around the 90th percentile for the year.
The VIX term structure is nearly flat at 0.995, not inverted.
The CNN Fear & Greed Index is 31, fear, but above 18 a month ago.
7 of 11 sectors are still above their 200-day lines; this is not broad weakness.

sectors.lead: Selling was concentrated in tech: semiconductors fell 5.1% and tech 3.2%, while defensives edged up.
points: The semiconductor ETF (SMH) is down 14% in a month and about 30% from its high.
Software (IGV) fell 2.2%; the AI selloff spread from hardware to software.
Dell (DELL) fell 7%; servers were also hit by industry debt worries.
Staples rose 0.3% and utilities 0.2% as money hid in defensives.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan opens today facing another round of US chip selling, but night futures did not crash: they rose 154 points.
points: TSMC's ADR fell 6.3% with a premium of about 11%; the local shares will open under pressure.
The SOX fell 5.3%; PCB and substrate names that hit limit-down Monday face another test today.
Foreign investors sold NT$70.2B Monday; their net short futures are 96,787 contracts and did not grow.
Margin loans fell NT$12.1B in a day and about 20% in 20 days; deleveraging continues.
The Taiwan dollar is near 32.9; more foreign selling would push it weaker.

watch.lead: Three hurdles in the next 72 hours: retail sales tonight, Nvidia earnings early Wednesday, and Anthropic's listing Thursday.
points: US October retail sales come out 11/17 21:30 Taipei; a strong print would push yields up again.
Nvidia reports after the US close 11/17 (early 11/18 Taipei); last quarter's revenue guidance was about $108B.
FOMC October minutes come out early 11/19 Taipei.
Anthropic is set to list 11/19 at up to $1.4T in value, which may pull money from tech stocks.
QQQ tier 3 is 645.71, 2.4% away.

regime.lead: By the rules, the broad US market is still in an uptrend and Taiwan is still a pullback: the S&P 500 is above its 200-day line, with 0 global systemic lights on.
points: Trend: all four S&P 500 trend checks pass; it is 1% above its 200-day line.
The Nasdaq 100 closed 3% below its 200-day line; the regime table still shows 11/13, and this is the second day below.
The TAIEX closed 0.8% below its 200-day line, only day 1 below, and the line is still rising.
Systemic lights: 0 global; credit, the economy and financial conditions show no stress.
The closest to turning on is the S&P 500 breaking its 200-day line, just 1% away.
Bottoming signals: none on in the US, 3 on in Taiwan.
History: S&P 500 dips like this are common; only 19 of 357 became 20%+ bear markets.
Taiwan usually fell further from here: 10 of 11 past cases broke −20%; the fast cases are too few to rely on.
What would change the call: 5 S&P 500 closes below 7,343 with a flat line means weak.
A TAIEX break below 39,858 (−20% from high) is a bear market by definition.
